issuing_body: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) (総務省・経済産業省)
covered_actors: Business operators and public institutions including national and local governments engaging in AI development, provision, or use
Business executives and management officers (経営者を含む事業執行責任者)
prohibited_practices: Developing, providing, or using AI systems or services aimed at unfairly manipulating human decision-making, cognition, or emotions, or premised on manipulation at a subliminal/imperceptible level
implementation_notes: Version 1.2 of Japan's unified AI Guidelines for Business, jointly issued by MIC and METI on March 31, 2026 (Reiwa 8), explicitly designed as a non-binding, goal-based soft-law 'Living Document' maintained through multi-stakeholder agile governance (via MIC's Conference toward AI Network Society and METI's Study Group on AI Guidelines for Business). Originally unified in April 2024 from three prior MIC/METI guidelines, it aligns with the G7 Hiroshima AI Process International Guiding Principles and Code of Conduct (including the OECD-hosted voluntary reporting framework) and references Japan's 2025 AI Promotion Act. It covers business operators (including national and local governments) across three roles—AI Developers, AI Providers, and AI Business Users—while excluding non-business users and data providers from direct scope. Practical implementation examples are provided in a separate Annex (別添).
